messages:
anita (sec-eng): Heads-up: rolling a small RBAC change to Console tomorrow 08:00 UTC. We're tightening the editor role so it can no longer overwrite billing and org-level keys. Expect brief UI gating tweaks. :lock:

sam (eng-platform): thanks. is there a migration plan for existing editor-held resources? we should emit an audit event for each coerced change so ops can reconcile.

anita (sec-eng): yes — migration script will map any editor-owned org resources to a new 'org-manager' role where applicable. script will write audit logs and tag with migration_id. planning to run in canary (10% of orgs) then 100% if clean.

maria (product-security): also: we discovered a permission-gating bug in the Console where the UI still shows the "Edit" button for non-editors in some edge flows (shared links + SSO fallback). not a backend permission bypass, but bad UX that could confuse users. needs a hotfix before the migration goes wide. :eyes:

josh (frontend): I dug into that. root cause is the client-side cache of roles not invalidating after SSO token refresh. quick patch is here: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/+/fix/rbac-cache-evict. key check is the component guard:

```js
function canEdit(user, resource) {
  // explicit: admin OR editor OR resource owner
  return user.role === 'admin' || user.role === 'editor' || resource.ownerId === user.id;
}
```

josh (frontend): I'll open a PR with tests and a small e2e that covers shared-link SSO flow. deploy-bot will run canary once merged.

anita (sec-eng): good. Sam, for audit logs — can we ensure KMS-decrypt events for key access are correlated with RBAC changes? we want a single trace for a migration action: migration_id -> user -> kms_key_id -> audit entries.

sam (eng-platform): yes. we can add a migration_id field to audit-log entries. KMS events already forward to audit-bus with resource name. I'll wire a short lambda to join events by request_id + migration_id and push to the security audit index. will need a KMS policy review for the lambda role.

maria (product-security): on vuln triage: there's a low-severity finding from the pen-test around stale role cache possibly exposing stale UI states — we should capture that remediation in the migration ticket and mark as mitigated after frontend fix + canary. also add a regression alert to Monitor for mismatched client role vs backend allow-check failures.

anita (sec-eng): agreed. i'll update the rollout playbook:
- preflight: run migration in staging, run canary 10%
- verify: audit logs show migration_id + KMS events + no backend allow-check failures
- fix: frontend patch merged and e2e green
- rollback: migration script reversible by mapping org-manager back to editor for flagged orgs

anita (sec-eng): tagging @sam @josh for action items. I'll schedule a 30-min window tomorrow 08:00 UTC. if anything odd, hit #incidents.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: console/fix-rbac-cache-evict -> env:canary -> started at 1793002000

audit-bot: audit entries will include migration_id=rbac-2026-03-21-01 and stream to security-index. KMS events matched by request_id when available.

sam (eng-platform): noted. i'll get the lambda policy PR up and the audit-join job ready. ETA 6 hours.

josh (frontend): PR opened. tests added. assigning to @anita for review.

maria (product-security): I'll add the regression alert and pen-test mitigation note to the ticket.

anita (sec-eng): thanks team. reopening thread if any blockers before 08:00 UTC.
